_exec_summary.SummaryText:
The Executive Summary below is provided to meet the requirements of the CalARP Submittal listed in 19 CCR §5070.3.

ACCIDENTAL RELEASE PREVENTION:
Fresno Cogeneration has developed a Risk Management Program and an Emergency Response Plan (ERP) to address CalARP Program requirements (19 CCR §5050 - §5160). Fresno Cogeneration has a long-standing commitment to worker and public safety. This commitment is demonstrated by the resources invested in accident prevention, such as personnel training and consideration of safety in the research, engineering, and manufacturing operations of ceramic matrix composite structural components. Fresno Cogenerations policy is to implement reasonable controls to prevent foreseeable releases of regulated substances and hazardous waste.

STATIONARY SOURCE AND REGULATED SUBSTANCE:
Fresno Cogeneration is located at 8105B South Lassen Avenue, San Joaquin, California, 93660. The regulated substances at the facility are anhydrous ammonia and 19% aqueous ammonia that are used for SCR systems. The anhydrous ammonia is used in the SCR system of Cogeneration Unit 4 and the aqueous ammonia is used for the SCR system of Cogeneration Unit 3. The maximum intended inventory of anhydrous ammonia is 57,270 pounds [lbs.] and the maximum intended inventory of 19% aqueous ammonia is 7,000 gallons (54,567 lbs.).

HAZARD ASSESSMENT SUMMARY / OFF-SITE CONSEQUENCE ANALYSIS:
Worst-Case Release Scenario Results Summary: Per CalARP and US EPA RMP Regulations, one (1) worst-case analysis for each regulated substance has been defined and modeled. Further details about the results can be found in the 2025 Hazard Assessment documentation.
Alternative Release Scenario Results Summary: Per CalARP and US EPA RMP Regulations, an alternative release scenario was modeled for each regulated substance. Further details about the results can be found in the 2025 Hazard Assessment documentation.

RISK CONSIDERATIONS:
Although the storage and use of anhydrous ammonia and aqueous

ammonia has inherent potential risks, and worst-case release scenarios can potentially reach the community; Fresno Cogeneration has recognized these potential risks and structured its safety programs to make the worst-case release type of event non-credible. In addition to the safety practices of the company and plant personnel to make this worst-case release event non-credible, it should also be recognized that there are inherent analysis assumptions that make the results of the atmospheric dispersion analysis appear worse than what would actually be expected during such an event (e.g., In the event of a release, sudden rupture and flashing of propane would be highly turbulent. Turbulence causes entrainment of air and the released vapor dilutes much more quickly than is shown in the model).
In addition to the use of conservative analysis assumptions that over-predict the effects of a potential release, other characteristics of the facility and site serve to minimize the potential risks associated with a hazardous chemical release, including:
 Automatic / Manual Shutdown
 Well Designed Relief System
 Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) is used by plant personnel, as necessary.
 The system undergoes periodic maintenance to reduce the likelihood of catastrophic failures.

ACCIDENTAL RELEASE PREVENTION PROGRAM:
As part of the implementation of this CalARP Program, key Prevention Program elements were documented and implemented by Fresno Cogeneration to manage process safety issues associated with the use of ammonia. Furthermore, common industry standards, policies, and procedures are currently utilized to ensure safe practices are being performed. The covered processes are regulated by the CalARP and US EPA RMP programs, as shown in Table 1 below. As a result, the anhydrous ammonia covered process is subject to CalARP Program Level 3 and US EPA RMP Program Level 3, and the aqueous ammonia covered process is subject to CalARP Program 2.

 Process Hazard Analysis

FIVE-YEAR ACCIDENT HISTORY:
For any accidental release meeting the five-year accident history reporting criteria of 19 CCR §5080.9, the owner or operator shall submit the data required under 19 CCR §5070.5, §5070.6, and §5070.7 with respect to that accident within six (6) months of the release or by the time the RMP is updated under 19 CCR §5070.11, whichever is earlier. From 19 CCR §5070.10: The owner or operator shall include in the five-year accident history all accidental releases from covered processes that resulted in deaths, injuries, or significant property damage on site, or known offsite deaths, injuries, evacuations, sheltering in place, property damage, or environmental damage.
There have been no CalARP-applicable releases Fresno Cogeneration in the past five (5) years.

EMERGENCY RESPONSE PROGRAM:
Fresno Cogeneration has implemented an Emergency Action Program (EAP) to prepare for potential incidents, respond to them effectively, and recover from their impacts. Employees are trained to the extent needed for their responsibilities. Fresno Cogeneration coordinates with local Fire Department and other first responders.
The CalARP Coordinator maintains the EAP that provides the evacuation procedures and notification procedures, evacuation routes, chemical health hazards, and mitigation procedures, which have been implemented to respond effectively to emergency situations that may arise at the facility. The EAP is reviewed and updated at least once pe

r year to ensure compliance with CalARP and ERP regulations.

EXTERNAL EVENTS ANALYSIS INFORMATION:
Pursuant to the requirements of 19 CCR §5070.7(l); the following external events analysis information shall be submitted:
 The types of natural and human caused external events considered in PHA 19 CCR §5100.2 or Hazard Review 19 CCR §5090.2.
During December 7, 2022, Process Hazard Analysis (PHA), plausible events were considered. General events external to the facility that can conceivably cause a release of Propane were addressed. For detailed information, refer to 2022 PHA Report.
 The estimated magnitude or scope of external events which were considered. If not known, the owner or operator of the stationary source shall work closely with the AA to determine what is required. If seismic events are applicable, the parameters used in the consideration of the seismic analysis and which edition of the Uniform Building Code was used when the process was designed.
A seismic safety walk-down was performed February 15, 2023. All findings are documented in the 2023 Seismic Assessment report. The magnitudes of the external events considered are detailed within the PHA Worksheets and were qualitatively risk-ranked by the PHA Team.
 For each external event, with a potential to create a release of a regulated substance that will reach an endpoint offsite, apply the expected date of completion of any changes resulting from the Process Hazard Analysis (PHA); major hazards identified; process controls in use; mitigation systems in use; monitoring and detection systems in use; and, changes since the last PHA.
 The date of the most recent field verification that equipment is installed and maintained as designed.
The most recent field verification of equipment was conducted on February 15, 2023, and included the system piping.

PLANNED CHANGES TO IMPROVE SAFETY:
The 2022 PHA study has been conducted to examine mitigation measures to improve safety at the facility. Planned changes

to improve safety are listed as recommendations in the 2024 PHA Report. Recommendations made during the December 2022 PHA are planned to be completed by June 2025 and will be developed into an action tracking log for the facility.

FLAMMABLES: WORST-CASE:
The use of flammable materials at Fresno Cogeneration is not encompassed by either the federal or state RMP requirements. Therefore, this section is not applicable.
